POLAR COORDINATESLE
The rectangular (Cartesian) coordinate system uses an ordered pair of numbers to represent the location of a point.
DISCUSSION
The first number in the ordered pair is X-coordinate and the second number is the Y-coordinate.
A point on the polar coordinate system is also represented by an ordered pair of numbers called a polar coordinate pair.
The first number is the radius. The radius determines the distance of the point from the origin along the polar axis.
The second number is q. q represents the angle of rotation.
When r is positive, the point is placed on the ray by moving forward along the terminal side of the ray.
When r is negative, the point is placed on the ray by moving backward along the terminal side.
When q is positive, the ray rotates counterclockwise.......
When q is negative, the ray rotates clockwise.

Rectangular coordinates can be converted into polar coordinates and vice versa based on the relationships from the unit circle.
X = r cos q tan q = Y/X Y = r sin q r2 = X2 + Y2
The first two equations are most helpful for converting polar coordinates to rectangular coordinates.
X = r cos q Y = r sin q tan q = Y/X X2 + Y2 = r2 + y2 r2 = x2 + y2
Simply place the r and q values from the polar coordinates into the two equations and simplify..
Now you have the equivalent rectangular coordinates.
